body:
## Short version The AMX kernels accept Muse Glimmer 30B's shape, 16 query heads per KV head, through one template parameter, and the kv_mul-4 kernels emit the same instructions as on main. Glimmer's 39 sliding-window layers then run on AMX instead of the AVX loop. On delphi-3bda with 8 users, Glimmer's decode rate per user rises by 4.4 to 15.2 % and its prefill time shortens by 0.6 to 8.7 % with the production attention mode (FPGA on the 13 full layers, CPU on the 39 sliding-window layers). ## Background Glimmer has 32 query heads sharing 2 KV heads, with 128 dimensions per head. The merge base (the shared ancestor of main and this branch) supports only kv_mul 4 on AMX. Its CPU attention therefore uses AVX for Glimmer. The interface header's Notes [AMX attention dispatch], [QK orientation] and [Tile stores write 16 rows] define the dispatch, layout and buffer contracts. Kernel naming and future group-size work are tracked in [#5021](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/issues/5021). ## How to review this PR **Does the transpose write exactly the intended query rows?** - `src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp`: check the lane-to-row mapping in `store_transposed_rows` against Note [QK orientation]. Lane stores are selected by `if constexpr`, without runtime condition checks. - `h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp`: distinguish the QK buffer's useful rows from the PV buffer's required 16 rows. - Verification: `t_amx_numerics`, case "AMX QK does not digress from the AVX dotter", checks both group sizes and leaves unused score rows untouched. The PV case checks useful output rows. The packer case checks zero padding. **Do dispatch and compiled kernels agree on supported groups?** - `h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp`: `group_heads_ok` and each declaration's `requires` clause admit only 4 or 16 heads. Eligibility also requires 128 dimensions per head and bf16 activations (the 16-bit bfloat16 format). - `src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp`: explicit instantiations must match that set. Direct kernel calls with unsupported group sizes fail to compile. An admitted size without an instantiation would fail to link. - `h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp`: all three kernel calls pass the model's `operation_kv_mul`. Partial pages retain the AVX path. - Verification: `t_amx_numerics` rejects kv_mul 8 and 32. `t_amx_dispatch_dtype` checks the model's group size through the executor using kernel test doubles. **Does the four-head path retain its behavior?** - `src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp`: inspect the four-head loops and separate per-instantiation scratch storage. - Verification: [Verification] records the kernel comparison, llama-3.1-8b token identity and performance results. ## Verification All runtime results use delphi-3bda. Tests cover the executable source at `4c4b7b8864` on 2026-10-18 (`round3.log`). Token and performance measurements use `5061623a34`, against merge base `6198824246` where specified. The initial, extended and test builds use clang 19.1.7, preset `native`, RelWithDebInfo, `BUILD_INGEST_MODELS=ON` and `TRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON`. Initial runs use `nix develop` on 2026-10-16–17 (`glimmer-20261016`). Tests and extended comparisons use a plain-shell build on 2026-10-18 (`glimext-20261018`). The nightly comparison uses main package `3751511dcc` on 2026-10-17 (`glimci-20261017`). Its target package uses the Debian-package preset, `deb`, outside Nix. These result records are on the test server, outside this repository. Benchmarks are not rerun at the current head. Below, the kill switch means `TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1` in the same binary. Layouts tp2/tp4 use two/four FPGA cards per model instance. ### Builds and tests | Configuration | Built test executables | Results: assertions / cases | |---|---|---| | AMX enabled | `t_amx_numerics`, `t_amx_dispatch_dtype`, `t_llama_unit` | `t_amx_numerics`: 17,425 / 4 pass
`t_amx_dispatch_dtype`: 3,694 / 1 pass
`t_llama_unit`: 265,452 / 67 pass | | Kill switch | Same executables | `t_amx_numerics`: 4,111 / 2 pass, 2 skipped
`t_amx_dispatch_dtype`: 3,694 / 1 pass | | `TRON_AMX_DISPATCH=OFF` | — | Insufficient data: no current-head build/test result in the cited records | What the table says: - The kill switch skips the QK and PV precision cases with "AMX unavailable on this host". The test process exits successfully. - The dispatch tests use fake kernels. They do not require a CPU with AMX support. - The kill switch has not been compared with a `TRON_AMX_DISPATCH=OFF` build. That comparison is not required for this PR. Clang-format 19.1.7 and `git diff --check` pass at the current head. At the measured commit, the four-head pack and QK instruction listings match the merge base. PV adds one instruction to form its per-thread scratch address. The remaining instruction names match, with different registers and offsets. [`glimext-20261018/preservation2.txt`] ### Token identity Each configuration generates 256 tokens, numbered from 1, for one user at temperature 0 with seed 1 and deterministic reductions. Here `run` is the measured commit, `repeat` repeats it, `base` is the merge base and `disabled` uses the measured commit with the kill switch. [`glimext-20261018/identity.txt`] | Model / layout / attention / prompt tokens | Run vs repeat | Run vs base | Disabled vs base | |---|---|---|---| | llama-3.1-8b / tp2 / CPU / 1024 | identical, 256 of 256 tokens | identical, 256 of 256 tokens | first difference at generated token 13 | | qwen3-4b / tp2 / FPGA / 1024 | identical, 256 of 256 tokens | identical, 256 of 256 tokens | identical, 256 of 256 tokens | | gpt-oss-120b / tp4 / FPGA / 1024 | identical, 256 of 256 tokens | identical, 256 of 256 tokens | identical, 256 of 256 tokens | | Glimmer / tp2 / FPGA / 1024 | identical, 256 of 256 tokens | first difference at generated token 6 | identical, 256 of 256 tokens | | Glimmer / tp2 / CPU / 1024 | identical, 256 of 256 tokens | first difference at generated token 54 | identical, 256 of 256 tokens | | Glimmer / tp2 / FPGA / 2048 | identical, 256 of 256 tokens | first difference at generated token 13 | identical, 256 of 256 tokens | | Glimmer / tp4 / FPGA / 1024 | identical, 256 of 256 tokens | first difference at generated token 31 | identical, 256 of 256 tokens | What the table says: - Required matches are run/repeat for every row, run/base for llama-3.1-8b, qwen3-4b and gpt-oss-120b, and disabled/base for Glimmer. Every required comparison matches. Other pairs are informational. - Glimmer's enabled path differs from the merge base. Measured score differences for the tp2 CPU/1024-token case are recorded in [#4444](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/issues/4444#issuecomment-6255615621). - **Insufficient data:** the other divergent cells lack comparisons of the gaps between the highest token scores. - The disabled llama run uses AVX instead of AMX and differs from the AMX-enabled base. This comparison is tracked in [#4444](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/issues/4444#issuecomment-6255615621). ### Performance The paired t statistic compares the mean paired difference with its uncertainty. Each band below is twice the larger of the two configurations' standard deviations. A change counts when its absolute size exceeds the band. Paired t values do not override this rule. All differences use unrounded means. **Production attention.** The measured commit runs 8 users with 2 repetitions per configuration. Full CPU-attention and prefill rows are in `glimmer-20261016/rt-results.txt`. | Glimmer layout / prompt tokens | Disabled TPS (sd) | Enabled TPS (sd) | Delta TPS (%) | Band TPS | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | tp2 / 1024 | 38.42 (0.003) | 41.89 (0.004) | +3.47 (+9.0%) | 0.01 | | tp2 / 2048 | 33.11 (0.032) | 38.15 (0.046) | +5.04 (+15.2%) | 0.09 | | tp4 / 1024 | 60.44 (0.168) | 63.08 (0.190) | +2.64 (+4.4%) | 0.38 | | tp4 / 2048 | 54.21 (0.018) | 59.74 (0.105) | +5.53 (+10.2%) | 0.21 | What the table says: - Every listed decode gain exceeds its band. - Prefill is 0.6–8.7% shorter. - CPU-attention decode gains are 6.1–21.2% for Glimmer and 5.2% for llama-3.1-8b against the kill switch. - At prompt 1024, AMX scores 72.1% of key tokens, FPGA 24.9% and AVX 2.9%. [`attn-stats-compare.md`] - Mean busy time per attention worker per model execution falls from 5.3 ms to 3.1 ms in the tp2 run. [`attn-stats-compare.md`] **Nightly configuration.** The whole-machine comparison uses Glimmer tp4, 8 users, a 1024-token prompt and 1,536 generated tokens, with 3 interleaved passes per configuration. The bands below apply the same rule to the saved pass results. [`glimci-20261017/summary.md`] | Configuration | TPS (sd) | TTFT ms (sd) | |---|---:|---:| | [Nightly reference](https://github.com/positron-ai/systems_test/actions/runs/38999609242), 1 pass | 78.69 (—) | 3696 (—) | | Nightly package rerun | 78.69 (0.13) | 3780 (14.42) | | Measured commit, disabled | 78.60 (0.25) | 3781 (8.13) | | Measured commit, enabled | 82.27 (0.28) | 3651 (9.59) | | Against nightly package | Delta TPS / band | Delta TTFT ms / band | |---|---:|---:| | Disabled | −0.09 / 0.50, inside | +0.77 / 28.85, inside | | Enabled | +3.58 / 0.56, beyond | −128.98 / 28.85, beyond | What the table says: - Enabled AMX improves decode by 4.6% against the nightly package (`t=33.1`). - Enabled AMX reduces TTFT by 3.4%. - Disabled AMX differs by −0.1% (`t=−0.4`), within its band. - A 20-second hardware-counter probe records 5.52–5.56 billion AMX busy cycles in enabled runs and zero in the other configurations. **Merge-base comparison.** These runs use 8 users and 4 paired repetitions, or 8 for llama-3.1-8b at prompt 8192. Llama uses CPU attention, and other rows use default FPGA attention. [`glimext-20261018/rt-results.txt`] A configuration passes the performance check when decode loss and prefill increase stay within their respective bands. | Model / layout / prompt tokens | Base TPS (sd) | Measured TPS (sd) | Delta TPS / band | Prefill change | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | llama-3.1-8b / tp2 / 1024 | 119.22 (0.11) | 119.35 (0.14) | +0.13 / 0.27, inside | +0.1% | | qwen3-4b / tp2 / 1024 | 133.61 (0.16) | 134.17 (0.15) | +0.56 / 0.33, beyond | +0.03% | | gpt-oss-120b / tp4 / 1024 | 96.77 (1.47) | 97.05 (0.35) | +0.28 / 2.93, inside | −0.2% | | llama-3.1-8b / tp2 / 8192 | 25.31 (0.06) | 25.24 (0.03) | −0.07 / 0.12, inside | −1.3% | | qwen3-4b / tp2 / 8192 | 61.74 (0.06) | 61.81 (0.07) | +0.07 / 0.14, inside | −0.05% | | gpt-oss-120b / tp4 / 2048 | 95.05 (0.63) | 94.85 (1.67) | −0.19 / 3.33, inside | +0.1% | | Glimmer / tp2 / 1024 | 38.34 (0.02) | 41.92 (0.05) | +3.58 / 0.10, beyond | −2.8% | | Glimmer / tp2 / 2048 | 33.01 (0.02) | 38.17 (0.05) | +5.16 / 0.10, beyond | −8.9% | | Glimmer / tp4 / 1024 | 60.46 (0.07) | 63.07 (0.09) | +2.61 / 0.19, beyond | −0.5% | What the table says: - Glimmer gains 4.3–15.6% decode TPS. - Glimmer has 0.5–8.9% shorter prefill. - Other tested models satisfy the stated decision rule. - The llama 8192-token decode change is −0.3% (`t=−3.7`), within the 0.12 TPS band. No further investigation of this difference is required for this PR. ## Open items No measurements remain pending.
